topic.angle: Four colours are enough for any map

body.claim: Any map can be coloured with just four colours so that no two neighbouring regions share a colour.
body.why: Mathematicians have suspected this since 1852, when Francis Guthrie noticed it while colouring a map of English counties. It was finally proved in 1976, and the proof was one of the first major ones to rely on a computer checking over a thousand cases. Some mathematicians were uneasy that no human could check it all by hand.

probes.question: How many colours are enough to colour any map so neighbouring regions differ?

image_brief.show: A coloured map with distinct regions

claims.claim: Title/claim: any map can be coloured with four colours so neighbouring regions never share a colour (probe 1 answer: Four)
claims.quote: no more than four colors are required to color the regions of any map so that no two adjacent regions have the same color
the conjecture was first proposed on October 23, 1852

claims.claim: Francis Guthrie noticed it while colouring a map of English counties
claims.quote: while trying to color the map of counties of England, noticed that only four different colors were needed
the four color theorem resisted until 1976, when it was proven by Kenneth Appel and Wolfgang Haken in a computer-aided proof

claims.claim: One of the first major proofs to rely on a computer
claims.quote: It was the first major theorem to be proved by use of a computer

claims.claim: Computer checked over a thousand cases
claims.quote: reduced the infinitude of possible maps to 1,834 reducible configurations (later reduced to 1,482) which had to be checked one by one by computer

claims.claim: Some mathematicians were uneasy that no human could check it all by hand
claims.quote: this proof was not accepted by all mathematicians because the computer-assisted proof was infeasible for a human to check by hand
